narrative:
The model predicted that you have a 56.9% chance of failing the bar exam on your first attempt. Because this probability is above 50%, the admissions system automatically rejected your law school application.

The decision was driven primarily by three factors, ranked by importance. First, your plan to attend part-time had the strongest influence, pushing the prediction strongly toward failure. Among accepted students, only 7% planned to study part-time while 93% planned to go full-time; the model sees full-time dedication as much more likely to lead to passing the bar.

Second, your third-year grades in law school placed you in the 3rd decile, noticeably below the average of roughly 6th decile among students who were accepted. This lower academic standing also pulled the prediction toward failure.

Third, your undergraduate GPA of 2.70 was below the 3.23 average of accepted students. In your specific case this actually worked slightly in your favor, making the model a bit less pessimistic, but it was not enough to overcome the other two factors.

Taken together, the combination of part-time study plans and weaker academic performance in both college and law school led the model to conclude you were more likely than not to fail the bar exam, resulting in the rejection.

You should consider reapplying with a clear plan to attend full-time and, if possible, strengthen your academic record before retaking the exam. Focus on full-time study and targeted bar-prep support to improve your chances on a future application. (248 words)
